From 1b9448b071caa7d10bb2569fabe3020a2c25ae59 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2015 11:49:59 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: quirk backlight present on Macbook 4, 1

Unsurprisingly macbooks have backlights, just the VBT doesn't seem to
know it in this case.

Reported-and-tested-by: Daniel Nicoletti <dantti12@gmail.com>
Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=88325
Fixes: c675949ec58c ("drm/i915: do not setup backlight if not available according to VBT")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v3.15+
Reviewed-by: Ander Conselvan de Oliveira <conselvan2@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446716999-1796-1-git-send-email-jani.nikula@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
index b0f23692346e..bcf227356f78 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c
@@ -14707,6 +14707,9 @@ static struct intel_quirk intel_quirks[] = {
 	/* Apple Macbook 2,1 (Core 2 T7400) */
 	{ 0x27a2, 0x8086, 0x7270, quirk_backlight_present },
 
+	/* Apple Macbook 4,1 */
+	{ 0x2a02, 0x106b, 0x00a1, quirk_backlight_present },
+
 	/* Toshiba CB35 Chromebook (Celeron 2955U) */
 	{ 0x0a06, 0x1179, 0x0a88, quirk_backlight_present },
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c`**
   - A new entry has been added to the `intel_quirks` array for the Apple Macbook 4,1 model. This entry specifies that the `quirk_backlight_present` should be applied to this model, indicating that the backlight is present even if the VBT (Video BIOS Table) does not recognize it.

### Relationships

- The modification addresses a specific bug related to the backlight functionality on the Apple Macbook 4,1. The patch adds a quirk to ensure that the backlight is correctly recognized and set up, which is consistent with the behavior of other Macbook models that already have similar quirks defined. This change is part of a broader effort to improve compatibility and functionality for Macbook devices within the DRM (Direct Rendering Manager) subsystem of the Linux kernel. The patch is also linked to a previous commit that disabled backlight setup when not recognized by the VBT, thus this addition serves as a corrective measure for the identified issue.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: quirk backlight present on Macbook 4, 1

Unsurprisingly macbooks have backlights, just the VBT doesn't seem to
know it in this case.

Reported-and-tested-by: Daniel Nicoletti <dantti12@gmail.com>
Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=88325
Fixes: c675949ec58c ("drm/i915: do not setup backlight if not available according to VBT")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v3.15+
Reviewed-by: Ander Conselvan de Oliveira <conselvan2@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446716999-1796-1-git-send-email-jani.nikula@intel.com

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the Video BIOS Table (VBT) does not recognize the presence of the backlight on the Apple Macbook 4,1 model, leading to the incorrect assumption that the backlight is not available. This results in the backlight not being set up, even though it is physically present on the device.

+

Reason:
The VBT does not recognize the backlight for the Apple Macbook 4,1 model, leading to the assumption that the backlight is not available. This results in the absence of a quirk for this specific model, causing the system to not set up the backlight even though it is physically present.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
/* Apple Macbook 4,1 */
{ 0x2a02, 0x106b, 0x00a1, quirk_backlight_present },
```
Reason:
This addition explicitly defines a quirk for the Apple Macbook 4,1 model, indicating that the backlight is present. By doing so, it ensures that the backlight setup is correctly executed, resolving the issue where the backlight was not being configured due to the VBT's oversight.
